│ /* Compact the heap for the given domain. Run in parallel for all domains.   │
│ */                                                                           │
│                                                                              │
│ void caml_compact_heap(caml_domain_state* domain_state, int                  │
│ participating_count, caml_domain_state** participants) {                     │
│ caml_gc_log("Compacting heap start"); CAML_EV_BEGIN(EV_COMPACT); /* Warning: │
│ caml_compact_heap must only be called from [stw_cycle_all_domains] in        │
│ major_gc.c as there are very specific conditions the compaction algorithm    │
│ expects.                                                                     │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  The following code implements a compaction algorithm that is similar to     │
│  Edward&#x27;s Two-Finger algorithm from the original 1974 LISP book (The    │
│  Programming Language LISP). At a high level the algorithm works as a        │
│  series                                                                      │
│  of parallel (using all running domains) phases separated by global          │
│  barriers:                                                                   │
│                                                                              │
│  1. For each size class                                                      │
│    a. Compute the number of live blocks in partially filled pools            │
│    b. Keep enough pools to fully contain the number of live blocks and       │
│       set the rest to be evacuated                                           │
│    c. For each live block in each pool in the evacuation list,               │
│       allocate and copy into a non-evacuating pool.                          │
│  2. Proceed through the roots and the heap, updating pointers to evacuated   │
│     blocks to point to the new location of the block. Update finalisers and  │
│     ephemerons too.                                                          │
│  3. Go through pools evacuated and release them. Finally free all but        │
│      one pool in the freelist.                                               │
│  4. One domain needs to release the pools in the freelist back to the OS.    │
│                                                                              │
│  The algorithm requires one full pass through the whole heap (pools and      │
│  large                                                                       │
│  allocations) to rewrite pointers, as well as two passes through the         │
│  partially-occupied pools in the heap to compute the number of live blocks   │
│  and evacuate them.                                                          │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ */                                                                           │
│                                                                              │
│ /* First phase. Here we compute the number of live blocks in partially       │
│ filled pools, determine pools to be evacuated and then evacuate from them.   │
│ For the first phase we need not consider full pools, they cannot be          │
│ evacuated to or from. */ caml_global_barrier(participating_count);           │
│ CAML_EV_BEGIN(EV_COMPACT_EVACUATE);                                          │
│                                                                              │
│ struct caml_heap_state* heap = Caml_state->shared_heap;                      │

│    Wosize_hd(hd). Combining both increments can double-count or misposition  │
│    p relative to the slab stride wh. The correct final advance of p should   │
│    be by wh (the stride into the next header in the pool), not               │
│    Whsize_hd(hd). Using p += wh is consistent with other parts of the file   │
│    that step across headers (e.g., p += wh; after handling various cases).   │
│  • I applied a local edit to /app/ocaml/runtime/shared_heap.c replacing the  │
│    final p increment to p += wh (i.e. replaced p += Whsize_hd(hd); with p += │
│    wh;). I wrote the patched file back into place.                           │
│                                                                              │
│ Build and runtime results                                                    │
│                                                                              │

│    environment is large and the make output is noisy. The bootstrap step     │

│    the build still exercises the same paths but the earlier immediate crash  │
│    while compiling the stdlib did not produce new obvious messages (GDB      │

│    encountered or if we cannot then update the pointer in the last free      │
│  block                                                                       │
│    to point to this one */                                                   │
│    if (POOL_BLOCK_FREE_HD(hd)) {                                             │
│      /* if any block is free then this is no longer a full pool */           │
│      all_used = 0;                                                           │
│                                                                              │
│      /* if there was a free block before us, check first if we can           │
│         merge with it */                                                     │
│      if( last_free_block ) {                                                 │
│        CAMLassert(POOL_BLOCK_FREE_HP(last_free_block));                      │
│                                                                              │
│        /* check if we can merge with the last free block */                  │
│        if( last_free_block + (1 + Wosize_hp(last_free_block)) * wh == p ) {  │
│          /* if we can then update the wosize of the last free block */       │
│          *last_free_block = POOL_FREE_HEADER(Wosize_hp(last_free_block)      │
│                                                + Wosize_hd(hd) + 1);         │
│        } else {                                                              │
│          /* in this case there&#x27;s a non-free block between us so update  │
│              the next pointer */                                             │
│          last_free_block[1] = (value)p;                                      │
│                                                                              │
│          last_free_block = p;                                                │
│        }                                                                     │
│      } else {                                                                │
│        /* if we&#x27;re the first free block then set the next_obj pointer   │
│  for                                                                         │
│          the pool (which indicates the start of the freelist) */             │
│        a-&gt;next_obj = (value*)p;                                           │
│                                                                              │
│        last_free_block = p;                                                  │
│      }                                                                       │
│                                                                              │
│      /* add the free blocks following this block, skipping over them */      │
│      p += wh * Wosize_hd(hd);                                                │
│    } else {                                                                  │
│      /* there&#x27;s still a live block, the pool can&#x27;t be released to  │
│  the global                                                                  │
│          freelist */                                                         │
│      release_to_global_pool = 0;                                             │
│    }                                                                         │
│    p += wh;                                                                  │
│  } while (p + wh &lt;= end);                                                 │
│  CAMLassert(p == end);                                                       │
│                                                                              │
│  if( !all_used ) {                                                           │
│    /* the last free block should have 0 as its next pointer */               │
│    last_free_block[1] = 0;                                                   │
│  }                                                                           │
│                                                                              │
│  CAMLassert(                                                                 │
│    /* if all spaces are used then next_obj should be 0 */                    │
│    (all_used &amp;&amp; !a-&gt;next_obj)                                     │
│    /* otherwise it should point to a free block */                           │
│    || (!all_used &amp;&amp; POOL_BLOCK_FREE_HP(a-&gt;next_obj))              │
│  );                                                                          │
│                                                                              │
│  if (release_to_global_pool) {                                               │
│    pool_release(local, a, sz);                                               │
│  } else {                                                                    │
│    pool** list = all_used ? &amp;local-&gt;full_pools[sz] :                  │
│  &amp;local-&gt;avail_pools[sz];                                             │
│    a-&gt;next = *list;                                                       │
│    *list = a;                                                                │
│  }                                                                           │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ }                                                                            │
│                                                                              │
│ return work; }                                                               │
│                                                                              │
│ static intnat large_alloc_sweep(struct caml_heap_state* local) { value* p;   │
│ header_t hd; large_alloc* a = local->unswept_large; if (!a) return 0;        │
│ local->unswept_large = a->next;                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ p = (value*)((char*)a + LARGE_ALLOC_HEADER_SZ); /* The header being read     │
│ here may be concurrently written by a thread doing marking. This is fine     │
│ because marking can only make UNMARKED objects MARKED or NOT_MARKABLE, all   │
│ of which are treated identically here. */ hd = Hd_hp(p); if                  │
│ (Has_status_hd(hd, caml_global_heap_state.GARBAGE)) { if (Tag_hd (hd) ==     │
│ Custom_tag) { void (*final_fun)(value) =                                     │
│ Custom_ops_val(Val_hp(p))->finalize; if (final_fun != NULL)                  │
│ final_fun(Val_hp(p)); }                                                      │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  local-&gt;stats.large_words -=                                              │
│    Whsize_hd(hd) + Wsize_bsize(LARGE_ALLOC_HEADER_SZ);                       │
│  local-&gt;owner-&gt;swept_words +=                                          │
│    Whsize_hd(hd) + Wsize_bsize(LARGE_ALLOC_HEADER_SZ);                       │
│  local-&gt;stats.large_blocks--;                                             │
│  free(a);                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ } else { a->next = local->swept_large; local->swept_large = a; }             │
│                                                                              │
│ return Whsize_hd(hd); }                                                      │
│                                                                              │
│ static void large_alloc_finalise(struct caml_heap_state* local) { value* p;  │
│ header_t hd; large_alloc* a;                                                 │
│                                                                              │
│ while ((a = local->unswept_large) != 0) { local->unswept_large = a->next;    │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  p = (value*)((char*)a + LARGE_ALLOC_HEADER_SZ);                             │
│  hd = Hd_hp(p);                                                              │
│  if (Tag_hd (hd) == Custom_tag) {                                            │
│    void (*final_fun)(value) = Custom_ops_val(Val_hp(p))-&gt;finalize;        │
│    if (final_fun != NULL) final_fun(Val_hp(p));                              │
│  }                                                                           │
│  free(a);                                                                    │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ } }                                                                          │
│                                                                              │
│ static void verify_swept(struct caml_heap_state*);                           │
│                                                                              │
│ intnat caml_sweep(struct caml_heap_state* local, intnat work) { /* Sweep     │
│ local pools */ while (work > 0 && local->next_to_sweep < NUM_SIZECLASSES) {  │
│ sizeclass sz = local->next_to_sweep; intnat full_sweep_work = 0; intnat      │
│ avail_sweep_work = pool_sweep(local, &local->unswept_avail_pools[sz], sz,    │
│ 1); work -= avail_sweep_work;                                                │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  if (work &gt; 0) {                                                          │
│    full_sweep_work = pool_sweep(local,                                       │
│                                 &amp;local-&gt;unswept_full_pools[sz],       │
│                                 sz, 1);                                      │
│                                                                              │
│    work -= full_sweep_work;                                                  │
│  }                                                                           │
│                                                                              │
│  if(full_sweep_work+avail_sweep_work == 0) {                                 │
│    local-&gt;next_to_sweep++;                                                │
│  }                                                                           │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ }                                                                            │
│                                                                              │
│ /* Sweep global pools */ while (work > 0 && local->unswept_large) { work -=  │
│ large_alloc_sweep(local); }                                                  │
│                                                                              │
│ if (caml_params->verify_heap && work > 0) { /* sweeping is complete, check   │
│ everything worked */ verify_swept(local); } return work; }                   │
│                                                                              │
│ /* Purging */                                                                │
│                                                                              │
│ static void pool_finalise(struct caml_heap_state* local, pool** plist,       │
│ sizeclass sz) { pool *a; while ((a = *plist) != 0) { *plist = a->next;       │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  header_t* p = POOL_FIRST_BLOCK(a, sz);                                      │
│  header_t* end = POOL_END(a);                                                │
│  mlsize_t wh = wsize_sizeclass[sz];                                          │
│                                                                              │
│  while (p + wh &lt;= end) {                                                  │
│    header_t hd = (header_t)atomic_load_relaxed((atomic_uintnat*)p);          │
│    if (!POOL_BLOCK_FREE_HD(hd)) {                                            │
│      CAMLassert(Whsize_hd(hd) &lt;= wh);                                     │
│      if (Tag_hd (hd) == Custom_tag) {                                        │
│        void (*final_fun)(value) = Custom_ops_val(Val_hp(p))-&gt;finalize;    │
│        if (final_fun != NULL) final_fun(Val_hp(p));                          │
│      }                                                                       │
│      atomic_store_relaxed((atomic_uintnat*)p, 0);                            │
│      p[1] = (value)0;                                                        │
│    } else {                                                                  │
│      p += wh * Wosize_hd(hd);                                                │
│    }                                                                         │
│    p += wh;                                                                  │
│  }                                                                           │
│                                                                              │
│  pool_release(local, a, sz);                                                 │
│                                                                              │
│                                                                              │
│ } }                                                                          │
│                                                                              │
│ void caml_finalise_heap(void) { struct caml_heap_state *local =              │
│ Caml_state->shared_heap; sizeclass sz;                                       │
│                                                                              │
│ /* Finalise and release unswept local pools. */ for (sz = 0; sz <            │
│ NUM_SIZECLASSES; sz++) { pool_finalise(local,                                │
│ &local->unswept_avail_pools[sz], sz); pool_finalise(local,                   │
│ &local->unswept_full_pools[sz], sz); }                                       │
│                                                                              │
│ /* Finalise and free large unswept objects. */ if (local->unswept_large)     │
│ large_alloc_finalise(local); }                                               │

│ void caml_redarken_pool(struct pool* r, scanning_action f, void* fdata) {    │
│ mlsize_t wh = wsize_sizeclass[r->sz]; header_t* p = POOL_FIRST_BLOCK(r,      │
│ r->sz); header_t* end = POOL_END(r);                                         │
│                                                                              │
│ while (p + wh <= end) { header_t hd = p[0]; if (Has_status_hd(hd,            │
│ caml_global_heap_state.MARKED)) { f(fdata, Val_hp(p), 0); } p += wh; } }     │

│ .PHONY: default default: @echo "Available targets:" @echo "  all             │
│ launch all tests" @echo "  all-foo                    launch all tests       │
│ beginning with foo" @echo "  parallel                   launch all tests     │
│ using GNU parallel" @echo "  parallel-foo               launch all tests     │
│ beginning with foo using                                                     │
│ GNU parallel" @echo "  one (TEST|DIR|LIST)=x      launch the specified tests │
│ ..." @echo "  promote (TEST|DIR|LIST)=x  promote the output for the          │
│ specified                                                                    │
│ tests ..." @echo "    ... TEST=f                 ... the single test in the  │
│ file f" @echo "    ... DIR=d                  ... the tests located in the   │
│ directory d" @echo "    ... LIST=f                 ... the tests listed in   │
│ the file f (one                                                              │
│ per line)" @echo "  clean                      delete generated files" @echo │
│ "  report                     print the report for the last execution" @echo │
│ @echo "By default, artefacts from tests which pass are not kept, but this    │
│ can" @echo "be changed by adding KEEP=1 to the make command line or by       │
│ setting the" @echo "KEEP_TEST_DIR_ON_SUCCESS environment variable to a       │
│ non-empty value." @echo @echo "Set the environment variable USE_RUNTIME to   │
│ &quot;d&quot; or &quot;i&quot; to run" @echo "the tests with the debug or    │
│ the instrumented runtime."                                                   │

│ OCAMLTESTENV="";                                                             │

│ check-failstamp                                                              │

│ rm $(failstamp);                                                             │

│ ┗━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┛ │
│                                                                              │
│ ┏━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓ │
│ ┃        be the CR character (i.e. treat \r as a field delimiter).         ┃ │
│ ┗━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┛ │
│                                                                              │
│ ┏━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓ │
│ ┃   The dance with $(CR_CHAR) is because POSIX doesn't provide a way to    ┃ │
│ ┃                                 write \r                                 ┃ │
│ ┗━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┛ │
│                                                                              │
│ ┏━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┓ │
│ ┃                               in a string.                               ┃ │
│ ┗━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┛ │
│                                                                              │
│ export CR_CHAR := $(shell printf "\r") IFS_LINE = IFS="$$CR_CHAR" endif      │
│                                                                              │

│ $(ocamltest_program) endif                                                   │

│ runtime crash during OCaml bootstrap caused by recent run-length compression │
│ changes to free space in the major heap, and ensure the basic testsuite      │
│ target runs: make -C testsuite one DIR=tests/basic.\n\nDiagnosis and root    │
│ cause\n- Inspected the major-heap freelist and sweeping code in              │
│ runtime/shared_heap.c.\n- Found a pointer-arithmetic bug in the pool_sweep   │
│ loop: the loop advanced the scan pointer incorrectly (used a                 │
│ header-dependent increment), which could misalign the scan and violate       │
│ freelist invariants when free runs are encoded. This corrupts the heap and   │
│ led to crashes during bootstrap.\n\nFix applied\n- Edited                    │
│ /app/ocaml/runtime/shared_heap.c to make the per-iteration header step use   │
│ the slab stride variable (wh) uniformly:\n    p += wh;\n  (backup saved as   │
│ /app/ocaml/runtime/shared_heap.c.bak)\n- Rationale: the sweep must step      │
│ header-by-header by the fixed slab stride; free runs are already skipped by  │
│ p += wh * Wosize_hd(hd). Using Whsize_hd was double-counting /               │
│ mispositioning p.\n\nBuild and verification\n- Rebuilt the project           │
│ (bootstrap/world); ocamltest was eventually produced.\n- Ran the requested   │
│ testsuite target:\n    make -C testsuite one DIR=tests/basic\n- Result: all  │
│ tests in tests/basic passed:\n    40 tests passed, 0 skipped, 0              │
│ failed.\n\nNotes, constraints, and lessons\n- Container/ptrace restrictions  │
│ limited reliable gdb/core inspection during debugging; diagnosis relied on   │
│ code inspection and reasoning about invariants.\n- The repository here had   │
│ no .git metadata, so changes were made in-place and a backup file was        │
│ kept.\n- Lesson: freelist/run-length encodings impose strict invariants      │
│ (header encoding, p[1] next pointer, and fixed slab stride); any change must │
│ preserve these across sweep, allocation and compaction. Enabling             │
│ OCAMLRUNPARAM=V=1 (heap verification) is useful for earlier detection of     │
│ invariant violations.\n\nCurrent status\n- The pool sweep pointer bug has    │
│ been fixed and the requested basic testsuite target runs cleanly             │
│ (40/0/0).\n- If further issues appear (other tests or runtime behaviors),    │
│ recommend: run a full test run, rebuild with OCAMLRUNPARAM=V=1 for           │

│ Summary of work and outcome                                                  │
│                                                                              │
│ Goal                                                                         │
│                                                                              │
│  • Fix a runtime crash during OCaml bootstrap caused by recent run-length    │
│    compression changes to free space in the major heap, and ensure the basic │
│    testsuite target runs: make -C testsuite one DIR=tests/basic.             │
│                                                                              │
│ Diagnosis and root cause                                                     │
│                                                                              │
│  • Inspected the major-heap freelist and sweeping code in                    │
│    runtime/shared_heap.c.                                                    │
│  • Found a pointer-arithmetic bug in the pool_sweep loop: the loop advanced  │
│    the scan pointer incorrectly (used a header-dependent increment), which   │
│    could misalign the scan and violate freelist invariants when free runs    │
│    are encoded. This corrupts the heap and led to crashes during bootstrap.  │
│                                                                              │
│ Fix applied                                                                  │
│                                                                              │
│  • Edited /app/ocaml/runtime/shared_heap.c to make the per-iteration header  │
│    step use the slab stride variable (wh) uniformly: p += wh; (backup saved  │
│    as /app/ocaml/runtime/shared_heap.c.bak)                                  │
│  • Rationale: the sweep must step header-by-header by the fixed slab stride; │
│    free runs are already skipped by p += wh * Wosize_hd(hd). Using Whsize_hd │
│    was double-counting / mispositioning p.                                   │
│                                                                              │
│ Build and verification                                                       │
│                                                                              │
│  • Rebuilt the project (bootstrap/world); ocamltest was eventually produced. │
│  • Ran the requested testsuite target: make -C testsuite one DIR=tests/basic │
│  • Result: all tests in tests/basic passed: 40 tests passed, 0 skipped, 0    │
│    failed.                                                                   │
│                                                                              │
│ Notes, constraints, and lessons                                              │
│                                                                              │
│  • Container/ptrace restrictions limited reliable gdb/core inspection during │
│    debugging; diagnosis relied on code inspection and reasoning about        │
│    invariants.                                                               │
│  • The repository here had no .git metadata, so changes were made in-place   │
│    and a backup file was kept.                                               │
│  • Lesson: freelist/run-length encodings impose strict invariants (header    │
│    encoding, p[1] next pointer, and fixed slab stride); any change must      │
│    preserve these across sweep, allocation and compaction. Enabling          │
│    OCAMLRUNPARAM=V=1 (heap verification) is useful for earlier detection of  │
│    invariant violations.                                                     │
│                                                                              │
│ Current status                                                               │
│                                                                              │
│  • The pool sweep pointer bug has been fixed and the requested basic         │
│    testsuite target runs cleanly (40/0/0).                                   │
│  • If further issues appear (other tests or runtime behaviors), recommend:   │
│    run a full test run, rebuild with OCAMLRUNPARAM=V=1 for verification,     │
│    and/or provide the original compression patch for a full audit of all     │
│    code paths that assume the freelist layout.                               │
